_note_habitat: The eleven terrain rows are the atlas's own biomes, so each carries a `biome` id and takes its label from i18n's biome_* keys. Roll 1 has no terrain of its own: it corrupts a habitat rolled again.
_note_encounter: d8 + d6, so 2 and 14 are the rare ends and the middle entries come up most. Roll 2 rolls this table twice and combines.

text.en: The party crosses paths with fellow travelers, such as pilgrims, merchants, or explorers.
The party suffers a temporary setback, such as a dead end, bad omen, spoiled rations, or damaged tools. Optional: The GM gains a Fear for each PC.
The Seekers-in-Shadow make their presence known, and the party must escape their grasp or stand and fight.
An extreme weather event occurs, such as an earthquake, a forest fire, a thunderstorm, or a blizzard.
The party faces potential adversaries, such as bandits, brigands, or mercenaries — or discovers warning signs of their recent activity.
The heroes find themselves in the lair or hunting grounds of a territorial beast or pack of creatures.
The heroes must overcome an environmental hazard or obstacle, such as a yawning chasm, rushing river, or quicksand.
The party encounters members of the Cult of the Two-Headed Coin, their agents, or signs of their recent activity.
The party discovers a wondrous or dangerous site worth exploring, such as a ruin of Old Valloren or a place of magical power.
The party gains a bit of good fortune, such as a shortcut, good omen, helpful resource, or lucky break. Optional: Each PC gains a Hope.
The party discovers a settlement or an outpost.
The party stumbles across a cache of loot or treasure.

_note_terrain: `days` is how long the party takes to move into a hex of this terrain.

text.en: Paved roads, stone highways, or raised paths allow swift and reliable travel. These routes are more heavily trafficked, increasing the chance of meeting merchants, patrols, or other fellow travelers.
Beaten trade roads, caravan paths, or wilderness trails provide steady passage. Though slower than highways, they're dependable, with only modest risk of delay or misdirection.
Narrow tracks, game trails, or tangled undergrowth make for slow, uncertain travel. Travelers risk getting lost, straying into hazards, or encountering dangerous creatures.

Cliff faces, quagmires, collapsing terrain, or trackless wilds push travelers to their limits. Progress is grueling, dangerous, and often impossible without climbing gear, strong magic, or sheer luck.
Dire fauna and carnivorous flora two or three times their normal size live here.
A black obelisk hums with the sorrowful voices of missing travelers.
A beast of bone and shadow stalks old ruins, calling out in the voice of a child.
A village that once burned down reappears in the light of the full moon.
A ruined wizard's tower holds books about the long-ago, the never-was, and the soon-to-be.
Geysers of wild magic erupt arrhythmically — random effects surge when spells are cast nearby.
A caravan travels an endless circuit, trading memories instead of coin.
The local wildlife knows the secret and safe pathways through this region.
A crystal canyon hums with unstable psychic reverberations, invading dreams with unwanted visions.
A shadowblighted knight challenges travelers to mortal combat. His curse is laid on whomever slays him.
A bell tolls at midnight, though no source can be found.
Lights flicker in the windows of a drowned city.
A broken bridge leads to another time.
A harpist made of light appears at a crossroads and demands a song in exchange for safe passage.
A storm of shadowblight hunts travelers like a thinking beast.
The earthquakes here are echoes of a chained giant's nightmares.
A storm of embers perpetually drifts overhead.
A ring of laughing mushrooms shares secrets with anyone brave enough to enter it.
Everything here appears translucent, as though only half real.
Travelers hear lullabies sung by unseen mothers.
A cloaked figure pays gold for tales of grief — no one knows why.
A sword of living fire fell into the earth here. No one has yet been strong enough to pull it from the ground.
A new caravan route allows trade and safety in numbers.
Invisible, impenetrable barriers turn the landscape into a labyrinth.
Within a canyon, gravity fluctuates and inverts itself unpredictably.
A spring bubbles with ink that heals wounds but permanently stains anything it touches.
A living cavern tempts passersby with tales of treasure within.
A constellation of ghostly lanterns floats through the air in mesmerizing patterns.
A mage's tomb wanders the land on giant mechanical legs.
Cracks in the sky show a different set of stars.
A hunter claims to know a cure for shadowblight but asks a dangerous favor in exchange for it.
Oversized fruits and vegetables offer an abundance of food to be foraged.
Spectral armies made of clouds wage war in the sky.
The earth bleeds when wounded by picks or plows.
A quartz tower splits the light of dawn into separate bands of color.
A bridge of spider silk spans a bottomless chasm.
The friendly hermit who lives here knows when others will die.
The blood-red lake is filled with eels who grant wishes — that those who make them come to regret.
A curse of magical silence befell this place.
A candle here burned through the Long Sorrow, and burns still.
A castle made of bone appears only at twilight.
Every night, a shadowblighted battlefield vomits forth undead armies to fight each other.
A tree with the face of a man knows the secret weakness of every living thing.
A city has been locked in magical slumber since before the sanctuary walls came down.
A ghost ship sails across land instead of sea.
A lost friend, relative, or companion was supposedly seen here.
A meteor fell to earth and cracked open, leaking strange life.
A field of magnetic stone holds fast anything metal.
An enormous clockwork machine lies half-buried.
Faceless merchants run shadow-markets.
A child of glass wanders the wastes, seeking their missing parents.
A labyrinth of brambles regrows behind travelers.
A village celebrates births with coffins, not cradles.
There is a shortcut here not found on any map.
A dragon's hoard remains mysteriously undisturbed, though the dragon hasn't been seen since the sanctuaries opened.
A tower grows steadily taller each morning despite no sign of builders.
Weapons can't be drawn here.
These lands hold evidence of an enemy's weakness.
Alchemists come from far-off lands for this region's rare herbs, minerals, and other components.
Schools of goldfish swim through the air.
A blind shepherd tends to flocks of shadows instead of sheep.
Fire burns cold and blue here.
The path is protected by wards forged by a nameless saint.
A gallery of stone figures stands, each a thousand feet tall.
A black sun traces its course across the sky every hour.
A bridge of flesh groans and sighs beneath travelers' weight.
A tree bleeds golden sap that hardens into cursed jewels.
A chained serpent begs for release.
The trees uproot themselves and walk around at night.
A chained door built into the ground in the middle of nowhere rattles at night. No one knows what's trapped behind it.
Ancient ruins offer shelter and salvageable relics.
A spectral orchestra plays in a ruined amphitheater.
A storm of crystal shards scours the land clean as it drifts.
A child living here claims to have memories of Old Valloren.
A cemetery grows larger each night.
The moon weeps silver droplets that burn the ground.
A warrior in golden armor battles never-ending waves of shadowblighted beasts.
A songbird guards a nest filled with magic rings.
A ruined temple drags travelers into its dreams.
A rainbow hums with power. Some claim it can be walked on.
Two doors stand side by side: one leads to wealth beyond measure, the other to certain doom. No one knows which is which.
The road vanishes behind travelers as they walk it.
A ruin of shattered glass offers windows into other realms.
A mountain floats high above the ground, green lightning striking its peak.
A mysterious hunter born from the land ambushes trespassers with living arrows.
A river of liquid light runs through here.
A colossus sleeps here, often mistaken for a mountain.
A plague of paper-eating butterflies terrorizes this region.
A gargantuan skeleton carved with runes sprawls across the landscape.
A cursed shrine answers any question in exchange for a year of life.
A never-ending storm carries the voices of drowned sailors.
The flowers here bloom in response to the goddess Aurelia's name.
A herd of luminous beasts crosses the land in silence.
A meadow of glass flowers rings in the wind. If its music can be deciphered, it tells the future.
Soldiers made of sand appear in the morning but crumble when touched.
A tree bears glowing fruit that changes the age of anyone who consumes it.
A pool of tears cried by an Aurelian saint heals wounds but deepens despair.
A crown of ice lies within a frozen palace and whispers promises of conquest.
A lone cottage stands with shadowblight trailing out of its chimney and into the sky.
A comet hangs in the sky but never falls. Rival religious groups argue about its meaning.

_note_sanctuary: One table per die, in the order the book rolls them. Political system 8 rolls twice and combines.

_note_nameElements: d100 twice, then one element from each result is combined. These are English name-building morphemes rather than prose, so they are never translated — the same way dice notation is never translated. Parentheses mark an optional tail: "Axe(l)" offers both "Axe" and "Axel".
